name: minijinja-named-slots
instr:
Please add named slots to MiniJinja call blocks so a macro can receive several independent pieces of content in one call. A call body may contain `{% slot footer %}...{% endslot %}` or `{% slot row(item, n=1) %}...{% endslot %}` at its top level. Slot parameters and defaults work like macro parameters. In the called macro, `caller()` renders the ordinary body without the slot sections, and `caller.footer(...)` renders that slot. For example, `{% macro panel() %}{{ caller.footer() }}:{{ caller() }}{% endmacro %}{% call panel() %}body{% slot footer %}end{% endslot %}{% endcall %}` renders `end:body`.

Each slot is a separate macro defined at the call site, available whether or not `caller()` runs. It captures call-site variables independently of assignments in the ordinary body or other slots. A `caller` referenced inside a slot is the lexical enclosing macro's caller, not the object containing the slot. Nested call blocks own their own slots. Slot results follow the existing macro auto-escaping rules, and slots expose the usual macro metadata under their declared names. Missing slots follow the environment's undefined behavior, so `caller.footer is defined` can detect an optional slot.

Slots are only allowed directly in a call body. Duplicate slot names in one call and the reserved names `name`, `arguments`, and `caller` are syntax errors. The existing `Template::undeclared_variables` API must account for slot bodies and defaults in both modes without treating slot parameters
